title: Replace competing world saves with authoritative serialized turn commands

blocker.details: This source editor can change game-project files only. It cannot edit the control shell, server, queue, predictionBridge, POST /api/game-state or worldStore.commit. Tools, processes, files outside supplied sources and external resources are prohibited for this response. The provided runtime has a full-state CAS commit bridge, not an authoritative command submission, acknowledgement, replay or resume protocol.

implementationRequirements: Use ordered, deduplicated input/turn commands processed by one authoritative serialized simulation. Preserve full-state CAS protections for any remaining replacement path; do not deep-merge world state.

Specify stable client identity, persistent operation identity, client input ordering, authoritative server sequence, accepted/rejected command outcomes, acknowledgement and reconnect resume semantics before wiring the client.

Make command deduplication and its authoritative outcome durable across restart. Define bounded retention and explicit recovery when replay history is unavailable; never silently discard unacknowledged input.

Predict eligible local input immediately, reconcile against authoritative sequence, then replay still-unacknowledged commands using the same simulation rules. Prediction must not generate authoritative rewards or repeat presentation side effects.
Retain pending input across reconnect and conflicts. Do not replace this with contention backoff, random delays, skipped held attempts, a ready gate or frame throttling.

Resolve proven simulation parity gaps before promotion. Preserve enemy turns, damage and death ordering, inventory, quests, generation, loot, crafting, trading, companions and every gameplay decorator.

Keep the candidate restricted to the isolated test instance until parity and acceptance evidence are complete. The reported movement-preview endpoint is prediction-only and is not authorization to use it as authoritative simulation.
sourceParityFindings: The supplied GulchWorldEngine handles move and descend, but calls an optional cave hook and does not encompass the complete gameplay simulation.
Gameplay semantics are distributed across Gulch.commit wrappers and GulchCaveEnemies.advance wrappers. Their actual call order is part of existing behavior and must be captured in reference fixtures.

Several gameplay decisions use Math.random or Date.now. Authoritative execution and prediction require explicit randomness and time inputs with parity coverage; independently rerunning these decorators is not deterministic replay.
Setup generators currently submit full-world updates from snapshots and timers. Their ordering and interaction with played turns must be included in the authoritative simulation design.

The runtime currently permits one pending replacement, previews one eligible movement, and retains only one short-lived buffered action. That is not a durable command queue. Removing its gate without a server command protocol would increase conflicting replacements.

requirements: More than zero eligible trials in every required held-input scenario.
No missing or duplicated input commands; retain an auditable input-to-command-to-server-sequence ledger, including explicit blocked and rejected outcomes.
Exact complete-world agreement at the same authoritative server sequence.
No unexplained end-to-end stalls exceeding 200 ms.
Record actual keydown-to-local-visible-frame latency separately, targeting the next frame or 16.7 ms at 60 Hz.
Record keydown-to-first-authoritative-tile, per-tile gaps, browser animation callback gaps, rejected acknowledgements, acknowledgement timing and sequence-matched peer-visible timing separately.
Compare A and B with B as the reference, documenting clock alignment, signed differences and uncertainty. Never subtract unaligned process clocks.
Distinguish client frame scheduling, host processing, server acknowledgement and peer observation. Pending duration is not ping; headless host callbacks are not device presentation FPS.
Preserve exact source/save receipts and recordings. Do not blend revision 199 and revision 200 samples or substitute a syntax check or single-browser smoke for acceptance.
